clue.text: Practical guidance given when Tom's in charge?

definitions.text: Practical guidance given when Tom's in charge?

parts.words: Practical guidance given when Tom's in charge?
parts.note: a rough working method, read whimsically as the regime of the tiny fairy-tale hero Tom Thumb

explanation.surface: Someone called Tom offers down-to-earth advice while running the show.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough practical method based on experience rather than theory is the idiom here; jokingly, it is how Tom Thumb would govern.

clue.text: Inexperienced when hostilities may be taken up

indicators.note: in a down clue taken up means read from bottom to top, reversing the word

parts.note: war is open hostilities between nations

explanation.surface: A novice when fighting might break out.
explanation.definitionFit: A raw recruit is green and untrained, so raw is a synonym for inexperienced.

clue.text: One mislaying lemon

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who loses keys mislays them; a lemon is slang for a dud or failure, as is a loser.

clue.text: Vacancy for a premiere

definitions.meaning: the first performance of a show

explanation.definitionFit: A job vacancy is an opening; the first night of a play is its opening night.

clue.text: Deprived of power, and adjusted to the loss

indicators.note: adjusted means changed and reset, so the letters of to the loss are rearranged

explanation.surface: Left powerless and having to come to terms with a defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A toothless law or body has no bite, i.e. no real power to enforce anything.

clue.text: The BBC doesn't begin to be free

indicators.note: doesn't begin says the first letter is dropped from the nickname

parts.note: Auntie is the British nickname for the BBC

explanation.surface: The national broadcaster does not start being liberated.
explanation.walkthrough: AUNTIE (or Auntie Beeb) is the affectionate British nickname for the BBC; 'doesn't begin' removes its A. 'to be' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie a captive is to free them by loosening the knots.

clue.text: Feudal code, of one in jungle work

indicators.note: in puts the one letter inside the run of jungle plus work

parts.note: bush is wild jungle-like country
to do is to work
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A medieval code belonging to a lone figure labouring in the jungle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jungle work' reads as labour in the jungle, but the two words are separate pieces that the one is slipped between; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushido is the samurai code of conduct of feudal Japan.

clue.text: Roué's death wish

definitions.meaning: a roué is a dissolute man, a rake; the 's stands for 'is', joining the two definitions
the wish placed on gravestones that the dead may rest in peace

explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Roué's is short for 'is', so the clue reads 'a rake is the gravestone wish'. 'Death wish' looks like the psychological term but means the epitaph's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Rip is an old word for a dissolute rake, and the three-letter abbreviation is the epitaph requiet in pace, rest in peace.

clue.text: Honest salesman university's taken on board

indicators.note: taken on says the board word is added on after the others

parts.note: rep is short for a sales representative
U is the abbreviation for university
a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A trustworthy salesman has been hired onto the university board.
explanation.definitionFit: A reputable dealer is honest and of good standing, a near synonym.

clue.text: Workers on the track or in the dining car?

definitions.meaning: railway workers who lay and maintain the track
jokingly, staff who set out dishes on the tables of the restaurant car

explanation.walkthrough: Railway track is laid in plates; in a dining car the same name fancifully suits those setting out plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Platelayers are railway workers who lay and maintain track; whimsically, people laying out plates.

clue.text: Scrubbed flat

definitions.meaning: called off, as an event cancelled by rain

explanation.definitionFit: A match rained off is cancelled, i.e. scrubbed; someone exhausted and colourless looks drained, i.e. flat.

clue.text: Sort of drawing, one among copies to be returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the assembled letters are read in reverse order
among says the one letter goes in the middle of the word for copies

parts.note: to ape someone is to copy them, so copies gives apes
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A drawing in which one item sits among copies awaiting return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' puts I inside APES to give APIES, and 'to be returned' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown ink, and a drawing made in it is a sepia, a kind of drawing.

clue.text: Oil is hard come by for such a dancer

parts.note: DERV is British slang for diesel oil used in road vehicles
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Fuel is difficult to obtain for a certain sort of dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: DERV is the British trade name for diesel fuel. 'come by for' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirling dervish is a Sufi devotee known for spinning in ecstatic dance.

clue.text: Deceitful wife producing such nonsense

parts.note: double as in double-dealing or two-faced
Dutch is Cockney slang for a wife, as in 'my old Dutch'

explanation.surface: A two-faced spouse comes out with gibberish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My old Dutch' is Cockney slang for one's wife. 'producing such' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Double Dutch is an idiom for incomprehensible talk or gibberish.

clue.text: Tip lees out, and it may be written off

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of tip lees are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pour the dregs away, and the matter can be cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written off' looks like cancelled debt but means written and sent away.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter is something written and sent off; an epistle is a formal letter.

clue.text: Sailor cleared of swearing and taking drugs

indicators.note: cleared of means the sailor's letters are removed from the word for swearing

parts.note: abusing someone verbally is swearing at them
AB is an able seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman, acquitted of foul language, is nonetheless on drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is using is, in slang, taking illegal drugs habitually.

clue.text: Where one might be below stairs

definitions.text: Where one might be below stairs

parts.words: Where one might be below stairs
parts.note: below stairs is the servants' quarters of a big house, so this is a servant's state of employment

explanation.definitionFit: Being employed as a domestic servant is the sense, the life lived below stairs in a grand house.

clue.text: Joy about first sign of blossom in flower

indicators.note: about means around, so the joy word goes round the first letter of blossom

parts.note: euphoria is intense joy

indicators.note: first sign of picks out the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Delight at the first hint of blossom on a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphorbia, the spurge family, is a genus of flowering plants.

clue.text: Parking objected to when introduced

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs
to resent something is to object to it

explanation.surface: Parking rules were resented when first brought in.
explanation.definitionFit: To be presented to someone is to be introduced, a synonym.

clue.text: Fail project to take English and go down in class

indicators.note: to take says the project word takes English on after it

parts.note: to fail to win is to lose
to project something, such as a shadow, is to cast it

explanation.surface: Failing in a project to take up English leaves one lower in a school class.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop in social standing is the idiom, from losing one's position in the Hindu caste hierarchy.

clue.text: Check-in slightly flustered youngster

indicators.note: flustered means thrown into disorder, so the letters of check-in are shuffled slightly

explanation.surface: An airport check-in leaves a young traveller a little rattled.
explanation.definitionFit: A chicken is slang for a young person, as in 'no spring chicken'.

clue.text: Started action against oriental leather material

parts.note: to start legal action against someone is to sue them
E is short for eastern, i.e. oriental

explanation.surface: Legal action was begun over some eastern leather.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede is leather with a napped, velvety finish, used as a material for shoes and jackets.

clue.text: Godfather of advertising?

parts.note: a godparent at baptism also bears the title used for a backer who pays for commercials

explanation.definitionFit: A godparent is formally a sponsor at baptism, and a business funding broadcasts in exchange for publicity is likewise one.

clue.text: Bracelets for devoted old husbands

definitions.meaning: slang for handcuffs, worn on the wrists
men like Darby of the proverbial devoted elderly couple Darby and Joan

explanation.walkthrough: Darby and Joan is a British byword for a loving old married couple; 'bracelets' is old slang for handcuffs.
explanation.definitionFit: Darbies is old slang for handcuffs, and plural Darbies are figuratively husbands as faithful as Darby.

clue.text: Sort of diver in South Island

parts.note: Cuba is a Caribbean island

explanation.surface: A diver on an island in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: A scuba diver uses self-contained underwater breathing apparatus.

clue.text: Colt and Winchester called for one of these

definitions.text: Colt and Winchester called for one of these

parts.words: Colt and Winchester called for one of these
parts.note: the guns were named after their makers, Samuel Colt and Oliver Winchester, so each is a thing named after a person

explanation.surface: Two famous guns were summoned for a particular purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A word derived from a person's name is the sense; Colt and Winchester rifles take their makers' names.

clue.text: Some try out hiking in adolescence

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few teenagers give walking a go.
explanation.definitionFit: Youth is the period of being young, synonymous with adolescence.

clue.text: Practical joke put right in a moment

indicators.note: in places the right letter inside the word for a moment

parts.note: a tick is a moment, as in 'just a tick'

explanation.surface: A prank gets set right within seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: A trick is a prank or practical joke played on someone.

clue.text: Dependent on tobacco, but in good health

definitions.meaning: read literally, hooked on powdered tobacco inhaled through the nose
fit, up to the required standard

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means meeting the standard, fit and well; read literally it suggests a snuff-taker's habit.

clue.text: Horse showing no love for the river

indicators.note: showing no means the letter for love is missing from the horse

parts.note: a foal is a young horse
O is love, the zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A horse has no affection for the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fal is a river in Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fal is a river in Cornwall, south-west England, flowing to Falmouth.

clue.text: Colour in fashion, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the word for fashion is spoken, and the answer sounds like it

parts.note: to fashion something from wood is to hew it

explanation.surface: A shade that's in vogue, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in fashion' reads as trendy, but 'in' is a link and fashion is the verb, to shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A hue is a shade or tint, a synonym of colour.

clue.text: Sort of very old man found in Lear and then embellished

indicators.note: embellished means dressed up and altered, so the letters of Lear and then are rearranged

explanation.surface: A primitive figure appears in a decorated version of King Lear.
explanation.definitionFit: Neanderthal man was an extinct early human, so very old indeed.
